pr_title: cgtop: Do not rewrite -P or -k options
pr_body:
--recursive=no will overwrite possible -P or -k option hence making the recursive disabling impossible.

Check what counting types the system supports (encoded in the ordering of our enum) of and pick whatever user requests but is also supported.

Fixes: #25248
pr_comments: Failure of "CentOS CI (Arch Linux + sanitizers)" appears unrelated (TEST-29-PORTABLE), whereas "CentOS CI (Arch Linux)" verifies that the added test invocations succeed.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

While extending our test coverage I noticed I can't seem to disable the recursive mode in `systemd-cgtop` even if I follow the steps from the error message/man page:

```
$ build/systemd-cgtop --recursive=no
Non-recursive counting is only supported when counting processes, not tasks. Use -P or -k.
$ build/systemd-cgtop --recursive=no -P
Non-recursive counting is only supported when counting processes, not tasks. Use -P or -k.
$ build/systemd-cgtop --recursive=no -k
Non-recursive counting is only supported when counting processes, not tasks. Use -P or -k.
```

I suspect this happens because the set count mode is later overridden depending on the cgroup maks:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/6c83054c0133eb53245e479d71589dceff76cf74/src/cgtop/cgtop.c#L927-L935

Is this expected?
